symbols.name: bit length of n
symbols.meaning: The rounded-up base-2 logarithm of n, which is the number of bits of n.
symbols.quote: Write $b = \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ for the rounded-up base-2 logarithm of $n$, the number of bits of $n$.

symbols.name: working precision
symbols.meaning: The working precision in bits, p = 6b, so that p = Theta(log n).
symbols.quote: Write $p = 6b$ for the working precision in bits, so $p = \Theta(\log n)$

symbols.name: padded box cell count
symbols.meaning: The number of cells of the padded box, a power of two with 4n/b <= T < 8n/b.
symbols.quote: Write $T$ for the number of cells of the padded box, the array the algorithm works on, a power of two chosen with

symbols.name: logical bit volume
symbols.meaning: The logical bit volume V = Tp of the padded box, which is Theta(n) bits.
symbols.quote: The cost table divides every term by the [logical bit volume](logical-bit-volume.md) $V = Tp$ of the padded box, so each term becomes a power of one size parameter.

symbols.name: size exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed positive rational exponent, 2^{-75} in the paper's choice, with d = Theta(p^epsilon).
symbols.quote: The exponent $\epsilon$ is a fixed positive rational number, not the tolerance $\varepsilon$ of the limit inferior.

symbols.name: chunk exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed positive rational exponent, 2^{-56} in the paper's choice, with K = Theta(p^{epsilon c}).
symbols.quote: The exponent $c$ is a fixed positive rational number.

symbols.name: resampling exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed rational exponent, 1/16 in the paper's choice, in the powers of the Gaussian and chirp rows.
symbols.quote: The exponent $\delta$ is a fixed rational number.

symbols.name: line-map factor
symbols.meaning: The factor of the Gaussian line-map cost, with alpha = Theta(p^{1/4+epsilon/2}).
symbols.quote: The factor $\alpha$ scales the cost of the line maps

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The width of the address chunks, in bits, K = floor(d^c) = Theta(p^{epsilon c}).
symbols.quote: Write $K = \lfloor d^{c}\rfloor = \Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ for the width of the address chunks, which are runs of consecutive address bits, in bits (the letter $K$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: largest axis length
symbols.meaning: The largest axis length of the padded box, a power of two, whose base-two logarithm is ell.
symbols.quote: Write $r$ for the largest axis length of the padded box, a power of two (the letter $r$ changes meaning here: it is an axis length, not the record length of the polynomial ring)

relations.quote: The cost table splits the [running time cost](running-time-cost.md) of the algorithm into separate terms, one for each kind of work.
The second row bounds the cost of the chunk exchanges that produce the [transform layout](transform-layout.md).
The first row bounds the cost of moves to their [destination rank](destination-rank.md).
The third row bounds the cost of each simultaneous [transform round](transform-round.md).
The fourth row prices the cost of the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) step.
The fifth row prices the line maps of [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
The cost table divides every term by the [logical bit volume](logical-bit-volume.md) $V = Tp$ of the padded box, so each term becomes a power of one size parameter.
